title: IronState Configuration
description: Schema for install/windows/site.yml and its per-machine (hosts/<COMPUTERNAME>.yml) and per-user (variables/<USERNAME>.yml) overlay files. A document is either the explicit mapping form ('tasks'/'vars') or, when 'vars' isn't needed, a bare list of tasks/actions directly. Overlays use the explicit mapping form so they can merge by key into the base file (see install/windows/README.md): 'tasks' appends, 'vars' deep-merges key-by-key.

tasks.description: Task/action list, executed in the order written. See README.md for the task/action model.

vars.description: User-defined variables. Merged with gathered host facts into a single flat context that 'when' conditions and '${{ vars.* }}'/'${{ facts.* }}' templating resolve against (vars win over facts on name collision). Host/user overlay files deep-merge into this key-by-key rather than replacing it wholesale. The same 'vars:' key may also appear in a package's own main.yml (see the 'include' module) to declare package-local defaults - bare top-level names available inside that package's own expressions only, with this (site-level) 'vars' winning on a same-name collision.

oneOf.description: Implicit form: the document root is the task/action list directly.

templateString.description: A single '${{ ... }}' template expression whose result replaces the field wholesale, native type preserved (see README.md's 'Template expressions' section for the full grammar). Typically a path - '${{ inputs.<key> }}' / '${{ package.state }}' / '${{ package.tags }}' / '${{ facts.<key> }}' / '${{ vars.<key> }}' / '${{ item.<key> }}' / '${{ <id>.<field> }}', optionally indexing into a list with '[N]' (e.g. '${{ example_task.results[0].rc }}') - but may also pipe through filters, e.g. '${{ package.state | default("present") }}'. 'package'/'inputs' are only meaningful inside a package's own main.yml (see the 'include' module); 'item' only inside a looped task (see 'items'/'with'); the rest are available everywhere.

state.description: 'present' installs if missing; 'absent' uninstalls if installed; 'latest' always (re-)installs / re-extracts. Inside a package's main.yml, this may instead be a single template expression such as '${{ package.state }}' or '${{ inputs.<key> }}'.

tags.description: Tags for use with ironstate.ps1 -Tags (flat matching - a leaf's effective tags are its own plus every ancestor task's, accumulated). Inside a package's main.yml, this may instead be a single template expression such as '${{ package.tags }}', which resolves to the package reference's own 'tags' array (replacing this field wholesale, not appending).

when.description: Condition(s) gating this task/action and everything nested under it (AND'd with every ancestor task's own 'when'). A single expression string, or a list of expressions (implicit AND) - matches Ansible. Bare dotted/indexed identifiers (e.g. 'foo.rc', 'foo.results[0].rc') resolve against facts/vars/id-registered results/facts (no '${{ }}' wrapper); operators: == != < <= > >=, and, or, not, in/not in, is/is not, and a '|' filter pipeline (e.g. 'value | default("x") == "x"'). See README.md for the full grammar.

taskItem.description: A task or leaf action. A grouping task has 'actions' (a list of taskItem, recursively - arbitrary nesting depth); a leaf has exactly one of the module keys below instead. Enforced at runtime (Tasks.psm1), not by this schema.

name.description: Label used in output. For a leaf, falls back to a per-module default (e.g. the package name) if omitted.

id.description: Registers this leaf's result under this name once it runs: '{ changed, failed, rc, stdout, stdout_lines, stderr, stderr_lines }' (Ansible 'register'-shaped; every CLI-backed module and 'shell' populate a real rc/stdout/stderr, others default to 0/''/'' unless they throw). Later tasks reference it with bare dotted/indexed paths in 'when' (e.g. 'foo.rc != 0', 'foo.results[0].rc') and '${{ foo }}' in templates. If this task also has 'items' (a loop), every iteration shares the same 'id': the flat fields reflect the last iteration, and every iteration's result is additionally available as 'foo.results[N]'. Leaf actions only - not valid on a grouping task ('actions'/'include').

failed_when.description: Condition(s) overriding whether this leaf counts as failed - same grammar as 'when' (a single expression, or a list, implicit AND), evaluated against this leaf's own 'rc'/'stdout'/'stdout_lines'/'stderr'/'stderr_lines'/'changed' as bare names (e.g. 'failed_when: rc != 0'). Without it, a leaf fails by default exactly when its handler reports a non-zero 'rc' (a thrown error also counts as 'rc: 1'). See 'continue_on_error' for what happens when a leaf fails.

continue_on_error.description: When true, a failed leaf (see 'failed_when') is logged and the run continues to the next task instead of stopping immediately - matches Ansible's 'ignore_errors'. The leaf's registered result (if it has an 'id') still reports 'failed: true'.

items.description: Materializes this task once per entry (Ansible 'loop'-style) *before* anything else about it is evaluated - name, tags, when, id, its module fields, or a nested 'actions'/'include'. Each copy gets '${{ item }}'/'${{ item.<key> }}' resolved against that one entry. Wins over 'with' if both are set. May also be a single '${{ vars.* }}'/'${{ facts.* }}' template expression that resolves to a list (e.g. '${{ vars.ssh.authorized_keys }}') - resolved before task-tree flattening, so the loop still sees a real list at run time.

with.description: A single reference value made available as '${{ item }}'/'${{ item.<key> }}' - like 'items' but materializes exactly one copy, without iterating. Ignored if 'items' is also set.

actions.description: Nested tasks/actions, making this item a grouping task rather than a leaf.

wingetItem.description: A winget package. Matched by exact package ID.

source.description: winget source to install from, e.g. 'winget' or 'msstore'.

basicPackageItem.description: A package managed by chocolatey, pipx, npm, or cargo.

package.description: Package name as known to the manager's CLI.

goItem.description: A Go binary installed with 'go install'.

version.description: Version passed as package@version to 'go install'.

egetItem.description: A GitHub release binary fetched with eget.

package.description: GitHub repo in owner/name form, e.g. zyedidia/eget.

args.description: Extra arguments passed to eget. '--to=' paths support '~' expansion.

gitItem.description: A git checkout managed with the local git CLI, modeled on Ansible's git module.

dest.description: Checkout destination path. '~' expansion is supported.

version.description: Branch/tag/commit to check out. Default is HEAD.

update.description: When true, existing checkouts are fetched/pulled to reconcile changes.

clone.description: When false, a missing 'dest' is an error instead of cloning.

force.description: When true, replaces non-git/mismatched checkouts at 'dest'.

single_branch.description: Clone a single branch when cloning.

cronItem.description: Cross-platform cron wrapper: manages Unix cron jobs on Linux/macOS and delegates to Windows scheduled_task on Windows.

name.description: Optional label/marker for the cron entry or Windows task.

special_time.description: Special cron alias determining the schedule.

user.description: Optional user under whose crontab this entry is managed.

env.description: When true, manage an environment variable line instead of a command line.

value.description: Environment variable value used when env=true.

insertbefore.description: Insert env variable before this variable name when env=true.

insertafter.description: Insert env variable after this variable name when env=true.

disabled.description: Whether the cron job or scheduled task is disabled.

environment.description: Environment variables to export alongside the job for Unix cron jobs.

cronUnixItem.description: Manage a Unix cron entry via the local crontab command.

name.description: Optional label/marker for the cron entry.

user.description: Optional user under whose crontab this entry is managed.

env.description: When true, manage an environment variable line instead of a command line.

value.description: Environment variable value used when env=true.

insertbefore.description: Insert env variable before this variable name when env=true.

insertafter.description: Insert env variable after this variable name when env=true.

disabled.description: Whether to disable the cron entry by prefixing it with '#'.

environment.description: Environment variables exported for this cron entry.

cronFileItem.description: Manage a system cron file entry (cron.d-style), modeled after Ansible cron_file behavior.

cron_file.description: Absolute file path, or filename relative to /etc/cron.d.

name.description: Optional logical marker name, written as '#Ansible: <name>' for idempotence.

user.description: Target user for command entries in the cron file. Defaults to root.

owner.description: Optional file owner (username or numeric uid) for the cron file.

group.description: Optional file group (group name or numeric gid) for the cron file.

mode.description: Optional file mode for the cron file (for example '0644' or 420).

env.description: When true, manage an environment variable line instead of a command line.

value.description: Environment variable value used when env=true.

insertbefore.description: Insert env variable before this variable name when env=true.

insertafter.description: Insert env variable after this variable name when env=true.

disabled.description: Whether to disable a managed command entry by prefixing it with '#'.

environment.description: Environment variables exported alongside a managed command entry.

iptablesItem.description: Manage iptables/ip6tables rules (modeled on Ansible's iptables module).

direction.description: Optional direction hint used when chain is omitted.

ipv6.description: When true, uses ip6tables instead of iptables.

ufwItem.description: Manage rules through the ufw CLI.

comment.description: Rule comment, when supported by local ufw.

advFirewallItem.description: Manage Windows Firewall rules via netsh advfirewall.

firewallItem.description: Cross-platform firewall wrapper that translates to iptables, ufw, or advfirewall backends.

backend.description: Backend selector. auto chooses by platform and available CLI.

comment.description: Rule comment for backends that support comments.

zipItem.description: A ZIP archive downloaded and extracted directly (no external tool).

dest.description: Directory to extract into. '~' expansion is supported.

creates.description: Glob patterns whose presence signals 'already installed'.

sha256.description: SHA256 caching for 'state: latest' so unchanged archives are skipped.

cache.description: Path to cache the downloaded archive's SHA256 hash.

owner.description: Ownership metadata applied to extracted files.

group.description: Group metadata applied to extracted files.

mode.description: Mode bits applied to extracted files (for example '0644' or 420).

symlinkItem.description: A symbolic link created from src to dest. A thin wrapper over 'file' (type: link) - see fileItem.

force.description: Replace whatever already exists at 'dest' if it isn't already the right symlink. Default true, unlike 'file's own 'force' (default false) - preserves this module's original always-replace behavior. Set false to instead warn and skip when 'dest' exists as something else.

owner.description: Ownership metadata applied after link creation.

group.description: Group metadata applied after link creation.

mode.description: Mode bits applied after link creation (for example '0644' or 420).

fileItem.description: Manages 'path' as a file, directory, symlink, or hard link, modeled on Ansible's file module. Unlike Ansible, the target kind is 'type' rather than an overloaded 'state' - 'state' here is always this codebase's usual present/absent/latest.

path.description: Path to manage. '~' expansion is supported.

type.description: What kind of thing 'path' should be. 'file' creates an empty file if missing (no-op otherwise); 'directory' creates it (and parents) if missing; 'link' is a symlink to 'src'; 'hard' is a hard link to 'src'; 'touch' always updates the timestamp (creating an empty file first if missing), like Unix 'touch'.

src.description: Existing path the link points to. Required when 'type' is 'link' or 'hard'. '~' expansion is supported.

force.description: When 'path' already exists as something other than 'type', replace it. Default false - warns and skips instead, rather than destroying whatever's already there.

owner.description: Ownership metadata applied after create/touch/link operations.

group.description: Group metadata applied after create/touch/link operations.

mode.description: Mode bits applied after create/touch/link operations (for example '0755' or 493).

copyItem.description: Copies 'src' to 'dest'. If 'src' is a directory, every file under it is copied recursively.

src.description: Source file or directory path. Resolved relative to the install system directory (install/windows, or the owning package's own directory for packages/<name>/main.yml) unless it is absolute, '~'-prefixed, or a URL. If this is a directory, a trailing '/' copies its contents directly into 'dest'; without one, it nests as 'dest/<src's folder name>/...' (rsync/Ansible convention).

dest.description: Destination path. '~' expansion is supported. A directory when 'src' is a directory.

owner.description: Ownership metadata applied to copied file(s).

group.description: Group metadata applied to copied file(s).

mode.description: Mode bits applied to copied file(s) (for example '0644' or 420).

templateItem.description: Renders 'src' through the given template 'engine' and writes the result to 'dest'.

src.description: Template source file. Resolved relative to the install system directory (install/windows, or the owning package's own directory for packages/<name>/main.yml) unless it is absolute, '~'-prefixed, or a URL - same resolution rule as 'copy.src'.

dest.description: Destination file path for the rendered output. '~' expansion is supported.

engine.description: Which template engine renders 'src': 'jinja' (sandboxed, block-capable - '{{ }}', '{% if/for/set %}') or 'gotemplate' (Go text/template syntax).

vars.description: Extra key/value pairs layered on top of facts/vars/registry for this render only (last-write-wins, shallow merge).

owner.description: Ownership metadata applied to 'dest' after write.

group.description: Group metadata applied to 'dest' after write.

mode.description: Mode bits applied to 'dest' after write (for example '0644' or 420).

templateSourceItem.description: A template to render - 'src'/'engine'/'vars' only, no 'dest'/'state' (the embedding field, e.g. 'blockinfile.template', owns those itself).

src.description: Template source file. Resolved relative to the install system directory (install/windows, or the owning package's own directory for packages/<name>/main.yml) unless it is absolute, '~'-prefixed, or a URL - same resolution rule as 'copy.src'.

engine.description: Which template engine renders 'src': 'jinja' (sandboxed, block-capable - '{{ }}', '{% if/for/set %}') or 'gotemplate' (Go text/template syntax).

vars.description: Extra key/value pairs layered on top of facts/vars/registry for this render only (last-write-wins, shallow merge).

shellItem.description: Runs an inline PowerShell command or a script file. Exactly one of 'command' or 'script' should be given.

command.description: Inline PowerShell command(s) to execute. Use a YAML block scalar ('|') for multiline scripts.

script.description: Path to a script to execute. Resolved relative to the install system directory (install/windows, or the owning package's own directory for packages/<name>/main.yml) unless it is absolute or '~'-prefixed. Mutually exclusive with 'command'.

host.description: What runs 'command'/'script', like a shebang line. Default 'pwsh' runs it directly in-process (no subprocess). Recognized presets ('powershell', 'cmd', 'bash', 'sh', 'node', 'python') expand to their executable. Any other value is split on whitespace and used as exe + leading args, e.g. 'npx tsx', so any script runner on PATH works.

extension.description: Overrides the temp file's extension when 'command' (not 'script') is used with a non-'pwsh' 'host'. Defaults to a sensible extension per preset host, or '.txt' otherwise - e.g. set to '.ts' for 'host: npx tsx'.

creates.description: Glob patterns whose presence signals 'already run'. If omitted, the command always runs for state 'present'/'latest'. For state 'absent', these paths are removed instead of re-running anything.

blockInFileItem.description: Manages a marker-delimited block of text inside 'dest', modeled on Ansible's blockinfile module. Only the text between the marker lines is ever touched.

dest.description: File to manage. '~' expansion is supported.

block.description: Content to place between the markers. Use a YAML block scalar ('|') for multiline content. One of 'block'/'template' is required unless 'state' is 'absent'; 'template' wins if both are given.

template.description: Renders a template (same 'src'/'engine'/'vars' shape as the 'template' module) and uses its output as the block's content instead of a literal 'block' string.

marker.description: Template for both marker lines; '{mark}' is replaced with 'marker_begin'/'marker_end', '{name}' with the identifier from 'marker_name' (see below). Change this (e.g. to use a different comment syntax) if the file's syntax doesn't support '#' comments. A custom template with no '{name}' token produces a fixed, unlabeled marker.

marker_name.description: Identifier substituted for '{name}' in 'marker', distinguishing this block from any other blockinfile task targeting the same 'dest'. Defaults to this task's own 'name', then to 'dest's file name, if not set.

marker_begin.description: Substituted for '{mark}' in the opening marker line.

marker_end.description: Substituted for '{mark}' in the closing marker line.

insertafter.description: Where to insert the block when the markers aren't already present: 'EOF' (default, end of file), 'BOF' (beginning of file), or a regex - the block is inserted after the last matching line (falls back to EOF if nothing matches). Ignored if 'insertbefore' is also set.

insertbefore.description: Like 'insertafter', but inserts before the first matching line ('BOF' for beginning of file). Takes precedence over 'insertafter' when both are set.

create.description: Create 'dest' (and its parent directory) if it doesn't exist. If false and 'dest' is missing, the item is skipped with a warning.

backup.description: Write a timestamped copy of 'dest' (dest.<yyyyMMddHHmmss>.bak) before changing it.

owner.description: Ownership metadata applied to 'dest' after write.

group.description: Group metadata applied to 'dest' after write.

mode.description: Mode bits applied to 'dest' after write (for example '0644' or 420).

lineInFileItem.description: Manages one line in a text file, modeled on Ansible's lineinfile module.

path.description: Primary path field for the file to manage. '~' expansion is supported.

line.description: Line to ensure exists (or replacement text when 'regexp'/'search_string' matches). Required for state present/latest. Supports regex capture replacements when used with 'regexp'+'backrefs' (e.g. '$1'/'\1'/'\g<name>'). Also supports inline templating: '${{ ... }}' (ironstate syntax), Go template '{{ .Key }}', and Jinja '{{ key }}'.

regexp.description: Regex to match target line(s). For present/latest, the last matching line is replaced. For absent, all matching lines are removed.

search_string.description: Literal substring match alternative to 'regexp'. Mutually exclusive with 'regexp'.

backrefs.description: When true (requires 'regexp'), 'line' may contain regex backrefs (e.g. '\1', '\g<name>'). If 'regexp' has no match, the file is left unchanged.

with.description: Optional context values for templated 'line' rendering. Keys are available as top-level names and under 'with' and 'input' namespaces for '${{ ... }}' (for example '${{ input.Version }}').

insertafter.description: Insertion location for present/latest when no match is found: 'EOF' (default), 'BOF', or a regex. Regex mode inserts after the last matching line unless 'firstmatch' is true.

insertbefore.description: Insertion location for present/latest when no match is found: 'BOF' or a regex. Regex mode inserts before the last matching line unless 'firstmatch' is true. Mutually exclusive with 'insertafter'.

firstmatch.description: With regex insertbefore/insertafter, use the first matching line instead of the last.

create.description: Create the target file (and parent directory) when missing for state present/latest.

backup.description: Write a timestamped backup copy (path.<yyyyMMddHHmmss>.bak) before changing the file.

owner.description: Ownership metadata applied to the target file after write.

group.description: Group metadata applied to the target file after write.

mode.description: Mode bits applied to the target file after write (for example '0644' or 420).

sshHostEntryItem.description: One ssh_config 'Host' entry. Field names may be snake_case/camelCase/PascalCase - normalized to the PascalCase OpenSSH expects (e.g. 'host_name'/'hostName'/'HostName' all become 'HostName'). Not validated against real OpenSSH keywords - the caller is trusted to know what they're configuring.

comment.description: Rendered verbatim as a '# <comment>' line above this entry's 'Host' line, overriding the owning task's own 'comment_template' for this one entry.

additionalProperties.description: Any other field becomes '<PascalCaseKey> <value>' (booleans render as yes/no). A list-valued field is singularized (trailing 's' dropped from the PascalCased key, e.g. 'identity_files' -> 'IdentityFile') and repeated once per entry, since directives like 'IdentityFile' have no plural form.

sshHostBlockItem.description: Renders one or more ssh_config 'Host' blocks from structured data (see 'sshHostEntryItem') into a marker-delimited block in 'dest', reusing 'blockinfile's marker/insert/backup model - multiple 'ssh_host_block'/'blockinfile' tasks can share the same 'dest' as long as each uses its own 'marker_name'.

dest.description: File to manage, e.g. '~/.ssh/config'. '~' expansion is supported.

hosts.description: One or more host entries to render, in order. May also be a single '${{ vars.* }}'/'${{ facts.* }}' template expression that resolves to a list.

defaults.description: Fields merged underneath every entry in 'hosts' - an entry's own fields win. Lets a set of hosts share common fields (e.g. '{ user: git, identities_only: yes }') without repeating them on every entry.

comment_template.description: Auto-builds a 'comment' for any entry that doesn't set its own literal one, e.g. 'Enterprise: {host} (orgs: {orgs})' - '{key}' is replaced with that entry's own field (a list joins with ', '). Any key referenced this way is treated as comment metadata, not a directive, so it's excluded from the entry's rendered directive list too (same treatment as 'host'/'comment').

marker.description: Template for both marker lines; '{mark}' is replaced with 'marker_begin'/'marker_end', '{name}' with the identifier from 'marker_name' (see below). Change this (e.g. to use a different comment syntax) if the file's syntax doesn't support '#' comments. A custom template with no '{name}' token produces a fixed, unlabeled marker.

marker_name.description: Identifier substituted for '{name}' in 'marker', distinguishing this block from any other blockinfile/ssh_host_block task targeting the same 'dest'. Defaults to this task's own 'name', then to 'dest's file name, if not set.

marker_begin.description: Substituted for '{mark}' in the opening marker line.

marker_end.description: Substituted for '{mark}' in the closing marker line.

insertafter.description: Where to insert the block when the markers aren't already present: 'EOF' (default, end of file), 'BOF' (beginning of file), or a regex - the block is inserted after the last matching line (falls back to EOF if nothing matches). Ignored if 'insertbefore' is also set.

insertbefore.description: Like 'insertafter', but inserts before the first matching line ('BOF' for beginning of file). Takes precedence over 'insertafter' when both are set.

create.description: Create 'dest' (and its parent directory) if it doesn't exist. If false and 'dest' is missing, the item is skipped with a warning.

backup.description: Write a timestamped copy of 'dest' (dest.<yyyyMMddHHmmss>.bak) before changing it.

logItem.description: Prints a message at a chosen level. Reuses the present/absent state machine: 'state: present' (default) or 'latest' print the 'install' message; 'state: absent' prints the 'uninstall' message. Either give 'message'/'level' directly (shorthand for the 'install' phase) or nest 'install'/'uninstall' phase-specific blocks.

message.description: Shorthand for install.message - mutually exclusive with 'install'/'uninstall'.

failItem.description: Unconditionally fails this leaf (non-zero 'rc') with a message - guard with 'when' to fail only under a specific condition, like Ansible's 'fail' module. Reuses the present/absent state machine like 'log': 'state: present' (default) or 'latest' fails with the 'install' message; 'state: absent' fails with the 'uninstall' message. Either give 'message' directly (shorthand for the 'install' phase) or nest 'install'/'uninstall' phase-specific blocks.

message.description: Shorthand for install.message - mutually exclusive with 'install'/'uninstall'.

exit_code.description: The 'rc' this leaf reports - applies to whichever phase actually runs.

includeItem.description: Pulls in packages/<name>/main.yml's task list as if written inline in place of this action (like 'actions:', but sourced from a file). None of 'state'/'tags'/'with' here are applied to the included tasks automatically - the package opts in by referencing '${{ package.state }}', '${{ package.tags }}', or '${{ inputs.<key> }}' on whichever of its own fields should receive them. Tags/when that should apply to every included task belong on this taskItem's own envelope 'tags'/'when' (which cascade down normally), not here.

state.description: Made available inside the package as '${{ package.state }}'.

tags.description: Made available inside the package as '${{ package.tags }}'.

with.description: Arbitrary key/value inputs made available inside the package as '${{ inputs.<key> }}' (dotted paths, e.g. '${{ inputs.<key>.<nested> }}', work for nested values).

factItem.description: Sets an arbitrary named value for later tasks to reference - registered under the 'facts' namespace alongside gathered host facts (bare 'facts.<name>' / 'facts.<name>.<field>' in 'when', '${{ facts.<name> }}' in templates - a user-defined counterpart to gathered facts, distinct from 'id'-registered results). Reuses the present/absent state machine like 'log': 'state: present' (default) or 'latest' (re)sets the fact every time this is reached; 'state: absent' unsets it. No real idempotency - a fact always fires when reached.

name.description: Name this fact is registered under, as 'facts.<name>'.

shell.description: Runs this command to compute the fact's value, instead of (or alongside) a literal 'value'. Always actually runs, even without '-Apply' - a fact has no real system side effect, so dry-run previews of later 'when'/'${{ }}' references need it to behave the same as a real run (the one exception to '-Apply' gating, alongside the fact's own registration below). If 'value' is omitted, the fact is set to the command's trimmed stdout. If 'value' is given, it's resolved *after* the command runs, against this task's own bare 'rc'/'stdout'/'stdout_lines'/'stderr'/'stderr_lines' (same self-reference convention as 'failed_when') alongside the usual facts/vars/id-registered context - e.g. 'value: "${{ stdout | dirname }}"'.

value.description: Any YAML value - scalar, list, or nested mapping. May reference '${{ <id> }}' / '${{ facts.* }}' / '${{ vars.* }}', resolved before being stored. Required unless 'state' is 'absent' or 'shell' is given (see 'shell').

mountFactsItem.description: Gathers the host's currently-mounted filesystems (Windows drive letters/NTFS mount points/mapped network drives; Linux via /proc/mounts or /etc/mtab; macOS via getfsstat) and registers them as a fact - a task-callable, on-demand counterpart to the fixed set of gathered host facts (see 'Facts'), mirroring Ansible's mount_facts module. Each entry has 'source' (where it was read from), 'device', 'fstype', 'options', and 'path'. Runs in the same facts-first dispatch pass as 'fact'. Reuses the present/absent state machine: 'state: present' (default) or 'latest' (re)gathers and (re)sets the fact every time this is reached; 'state: absent' unsets it.

name.description: Name this fact is registered under, as 'facts.<name>'. Defaults to 'mounts'.

timeout.description: Maximum seconds to spend gathering before failing this task. 0 (or omitted) means no bound. Mainly matters on Windows, where an unreachable mapped network drive can otherwise stall indefinitely.

assertItem.description: Fails this task unless every 'that' condition holds. 'that' uses the same bare-expression grammar as 'when' (dotted/indexed identifiers, comparisons, and/or/not, in/not in, is/is not, '|' filters), evaluated against facts/vars/id-registered results. A failure becomes this leaf's 'rc: 1' (message in 'stderr'), a pass becomes 'rc: 0' (message in 'stdout') - ordinary 'failed_when'/'continue_on_error' apply on top of that like any other leaf. Always actually evaluated, even without '-Apply' - the check has no system side effect to skip in a dry run.

that.description: Condition(s) that must all be true. A single expression string, or a list of expressions (implicit AND) - matches 'when'.

fail_msg.description: Error message used verbatim when one or more 'that' conditions are false. Without it, a message is built from the task's name and every failing condition.

success_msg.description: Message used verbatim when every 'that' condition is true. Without it, a message is built from the task's name and the number of conditions checked.

asyncItem.description: Runs 'tasks' (a nested task/action list, same grammar as the top-level 'tasks:') in the background and returns immediately, without waiting for it to finish - the rest of the playbook continues right away. A later 'wait_for' task references this job by its 'id' to observe completion. Always actually runs, even without '-Apply' - starting the background job has no meaningful dry-run preview. Note: 'id' here is this async job's own handle for 'wait_for' - distinct from this task's top-level 'id' (which, like any task, registers this leaf's own immediate 'started' result, not the background job's eventual outcome). The nested tasks run against a snapshot of facts/vars/id-registered results taken when this task runs, not the live, still-changing state the rest of the run sees - a fact or id registered *inside* the background tasks is not visible to any other task, only via 'wait_for'.

id.description: Job handle name. 'wait_for' tasks reference this in their own 'for' list to wait for this job to finish.

tasks.description: Task/action list to run in the background, in order - same grammar as the top-level 'tasks:' (leaves and/or grouping 'actions').

waitForItem.description: Blocks until every async job named in 'for' has finished and/or 'condition' becomes true (both, if both given - implicit AND), polling every 'interval' seconds, up to 'timeout' seconds. Fails ('rc: 1') if the timeout elapses first, or if any awaited async job itself failed. 'condition' uses the same bare-expression grammar as 'when'/'that', evaluated against facts/vars/id-registered results captured when this task runs (not re-gathered each poll) - only useful when driven by a filter that itself checks live state (e.g. a script filter), or combined with 'for'. Always actually runs, even without '-Apply'.

for.description: Async job id(s) (see the 'async' module's 'id') to wait for completion of. A single string, or a list (waits for all of them).

condition.description: Condition(s) that must all be true before continuing - same grammar as 'when'/'that'. A single expression string, or a list of expressions (implicit AND).

timeout.description: Maximum seconds to wait before failing this task.

registryValueItem.description: One named value to write under a registry.path.

type.description: One of String, ExpandString, Binary, DWord, MultiString, QWord (matched case-insensitively - 'DWORD'/'QWORD' work too).

value.description: Matches 'type': a scalar for String/ExpandString/DWord/QWord, a list for MultiString (strings) or Binary (byte values 0-255). Required unless the registry item's 'state' is 'absent'.

registryItem.description: Writes one or more named values under a single registry key.

path.description: Registry key path. Supports hive shortcuts HKLM/HKCU/HKCR/HKU/HKCC and their HKEY_* full names (e.g. 'HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\...'), with or without a trailing ':' or forward slashes. HKCR/HKU/HKCC are mounted as PSDrives on first use if not already present.

values.description: One or more named values to write under 'path'.

owner.description: Windows ACL owner to apply to the target registry key.

group.description: Windows ACL group to apply to the target registry key.

scheduledTaskActionItem.description: One Task Scheduler action (run a program). Only plain executable actions are supported (not COM-handler/email actions).

execute.description: Path to the executable/script to run.

working_directory.description: Working directory the action runs from.

scheduledTaskTriggerItem.description: One Task Scheduler trigger. 'type' selects which of the other fields apply - enforced at runtime, not by this schema (see modules/Handlers/ScheduledTask.psm1). Duration-like fields ('delay', 'random_delay', 'repetition_interval', 'repetition_duration') accept either an ISO 8601 duration ('PT30S', 'P1D') or a plain .NET TimeSpan string ('00:00:30', '1.00:00:00').

type.description: 'logon': fires when a user logs on (any user, or a specific 'user_id'). 'startup': fires at system boot. 'once': fires once at 'at'. 'daily': fires at the time-of-day in 'at', every 'days_interval' days. 'weekly': fires at the time-of-day in 'at', on 'days_of_week', every 'weeks_interval' weeks.

user_id.description: 'logon' only - restricts the trigger to a specific user. Omit to fire for any user.

at.description: 'once'/'daily'/'weekly' only. Full date+time (e.g. '2026-08-15T09:00:00') for 'once' - only the time-of-day portion is used for 'daily'/'weekly'.

delay.description: 'logon'/'startup' only - wait this long after the trigger condition before actually running.

random_delay.description: 'once'/'daily'/'weekly'/'logon'/'startup' - randomize the actual start time by up to this much, to avoid many machines firing at the exact same instant.

repetition_interval.description: 'once'/'daily'/'weekly' - re-run every this-often after the initial fire, for the duration in 'repetition_duration'.

scheduledTaskPrincipalItem.description: Which account the task runs as. Omit the whole 'principal' block to run as the current user with standard rights; when given, only the fields you declare are managed/compared (like 'settings' below).

user_id.description: Account to run as, e.g. a username, 'SYSTEM', or 'NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM'. Mutually exclusive with 'group_id'.

group_id.description: Group to run as instead of a single user. Mutually exclusive with 'user_id'.

logon_type.description: 'Password' additionally requires 'user_id' and 'password_env'. A stored task password can't be read back, so idempotency can't detect a drifted password - only 'state: latest' is guaranteed to re-apply one.

run_level.description: 'Highest' runs elevated ("Run with highest privileges" in Task Scheduler's UI).

password_env.description: Name of an environment variable (populated via this repo's own .env/.secrets loading - see README.md) holding the account's password. Only used when 'logon_type' is 'Password'; never write a plaintext password here.

scheduledTaskSettingsItem.description: Task-level settings. Partial-declare like 'registry's 'values' - only the keys listed here are managed/compared; everything else is left at Task Scheduler's own defaults.

start_when_available.description: Run as soon as possible after a scheduled start is missed (e.g. the machine was off).

wake_to_run.description: Wake the machine from sleep to run this task.

multiple_instances.description: What to do if the task is triggered again while already running.

restart_count.description: How many times to retry on failure. Task Scheduler silently ignores this unless 'restart_interval' is also set - declare both together.

execution_time_limit.description: Kill the task if it runs longer than this. 'PT0S' means no limit.

restart_interval.description: Delay between retries when 'restart_count' is set.

delete_expired_task_after.description: Automatically delete the task this long after its last trigger expires (only meaningful for a task with an 'once'/'daily'/'weekly' end boundary).

scheduledTaskItem.description: A Windows Task Scheduler task, managed via generated XML and schtasks.exe.

path.description: Task folder (Task Scheduler's TaskPath), e.g. '\MyApps\'. Normalized to always start/end with '\'.

actions.description: Required unless 'state: absent'. One or more programs to run, in order.

triggers.description: Optional - omit for a manual/on-demand-only task.

owner.description: Alias for principal.user_id when principal.user_id is omitted.

group.description: Alias for principal.group_id when principal.group_id is omitted.

system.description: Create as a system group where supported.

password_env.description: Environment variable name containing the password.

system.description: Create as a system account where supported.

remove_home.description: Linux: remove home directory on delete.

pathItem.description: Ensures directories are present on (or absent from) the current user's persistent PATH environment variable (User scope, no admin required). Also updates the current process's PATH for entries it adds/removes, so later tasks in the same run can find them immediately.

paths.description: Directories to ensure on PATH. '~' expansion is supported.
